subject: NimbusHealth: sudden inference latency and 5xx increase — urgent
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: john.park@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2027-05-05T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden spike in inference latency and 5xxs — happening since 07:50 UTC

Hi Dylan,

We're seeing a sharp regression across our production endpoints since ~07:50 UTC:
- Median tail latency for text-generation calls jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s.
- 5xx error rate increased from 0.2% to ~6%.
- Throughput has dropped ~35% (backpressure on client-side).

We immediately validated on our side (retries, client-side timeouts). Server traces we can share show a pattern of repeated TCP SYN retries followed by RSTs between our VPC and Redwood's egress. We uploaded a small trace bundle here: https://s3.amazonaws.com/nimbus-support/traces/20270505/traces.tar.gz (pcap + request ids). I've attached a pcap snippet and a list of example request IDs (req_ids-20270505.txt).

This is customer-impacting and executive attention is requested — please confirm receipt and initial ETA. If you want us to open a support ticket with our cloud provider, we will.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Sr. Platform Engineer, NimbusHealth
elena.ruiz@nimbushealth.com

Elena — thanks for the quick alert and uploads, I'm pulling this in as P0. Confirming we received the traces.

Immediate asks so we can triage faster:
- Can you confirm whether this is limited to one region/peering (us-west-2) or cross-region?
- Any recent config changes (peering, BGP, firewall rules) on your side in the last 24h?
- I've started a collection on our egress nodes; please keep the req_ids file handy.

We'll run parallel investigations:
- Network (Jonas) will look at peering/BGP/session resets.
- Edge proxy + firewall (Vanessa) will check for proxy queueing or session exhaustion.
- Marissa will surface any observed model-serving degradation or runtime queue pileup.

I'll get an exec note out in the next hour. Will keep you posted every 60 minutes or on new findings.

—Dylan

Date: 2027-05-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: NimbusHealth P0 — initial triage plan

Team — forwarding customer report (attached). High priority: production inference latency + 5xxs; customer reports TCP SYN retries and RSTs between our egress and their VPC peering. Executive wants an ETA.

Triage hypothesis (ordered):
1) Peering session micro-flaps or asymmetric routing causing retransmits and higher RTTs.
2) DNS resolution anomalies causing intermittent resolution failures to egress proxies (NXDOMAIN/timeout observed in similar incidents).
3) Firewall/proxy session limits on their transit path causing connection drops and 5xxs.

Immediate actions:
- Jonas: pull eBPF/tcpdump from the specific egress nodes mentioned in the traces (I put req_ids-20270505.txt into our shared S3). Check for RST rates, retransmit patterns, and TCP handshake times. (owner: Jonas, ETA 45m)
- Vanessa: check proxy queueing metrics and firewall session table saturation across the egress cluster serving us-west-2. Capture last 3 hours of proxy logs and correlate to request IDs. (owner: Vanessa, ETA 60m)
- Marissa: confirm whether model servers are healthy and not causing internal backpressure that could surface as 502/504. Pull internal request latencies to rule out application layer. (owner: Marissa, ETA 45m)

Communications: I'll prepare an exec-facing summary for the customer and copy Vivek. If we determine it's peering/BGP, we should prepare to coordinate with their cloud partner (I've included netops@aws-partner.example.com in participant list).

Attachments for ops: req_ids-20270505.txt, nimbus-pcap-snippet.txt (attached to this thread).

Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-05T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: NimbusHealth P0 — initial triage plan

Update from our end after running the first-pass correlation:
- Jonas' packet captures (egress cluster n-17,n-19) show a pattern: elevated SYN retransmits followed by RSTs targeting NimbusHealth's peering ASN. RTTs spike from ~30ms -> ~950ms in affected windows.
- DNS lookups for our egress proxy hostnames resolved intermittently to older IPs (TTL expiry/propagation window) — there are ~3 spikes of NXDOMAIN/timeout aligned with the highest 5xx windows.
- Proxy metrics: queue depth increased by ~400% on nodes handling the Nimbus prefix for ~6 minutes; session table entries hit 92% on a subset of NAT/firewall devices (likely aged connections being reset).

Preliminary root cause (most likely): transient peering path instability combined with a DNS propagation/resolve window leading to mismatched egress IPs and session resets at the firewall — result is handshake failures and 5xxs.

Recommended mitigations (short term):
1) Trigger temporary BGP AS path weight adjustment to prefer alternate peering (jonas to coordinate with netops).
2) Increase firewall session table capacity on affected devices (Vanessa to submit infra change and schedule quick increase).
3) TTL/registry: ask Nimbus to keep a slightly longer DNS TTL during the mitigation window or coordinate a DNS hold to avoid mid-change resolves.

I'll draft the exec note for Dylan to send to Nimbus (2-paragraph summary + action items + ETA). If the customer requires immediate SLA credits, we should route through sales/finance after stabilization.

—Marissa
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: egress-traces.tar.gz (short capture files).
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>, John Park <john.park@nimbushealth.com>

Date: 2027-05-05T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: NimbusHealth — executive update and next steps (ETA ~3h stabilization)

Elena/John — quick executive update and immediate plan after our investigations:

What we saw: transient peering/route instability combined with intermittent DNS resolve windows resulted in mismatched egress IPs and session table pressure on firewall/NAT devices. This produced repeated handshake failures (SYN retransmits -> RST) and a burst of 5xxs.

Actions we are taking now (in progress / ETA ~3 hours for initial stabilization):
- Jonas coordinating an AS path preference flip to move traffic to an alternate peering (reduces chance of the current path’s micro-flaps).
- Vanessa increasing session table capacity and rebalancing proxy routing to reduce queueing on affected nodes.
- Marissa continuing correlation for any application-level signal; so far model-serving looks healthy.

Temporary mitigations recommended on your side: hold DNS changes and, if possible, extend TTL by +300s for the affected hostnames while we stabilize. We will coordinate with netops@aws-partner.example.com if we need their intervention for peering/BGP confirmation.

We understand the business impact and Vivek (cc'd) is aware. After stabilization we will share: a) a timeline of root cause evidence, b) a postmortem with recommended durable fixes (peering resilience + DNS change process), and c) a proposed service credit if you were materially impacted (we'll start that conversation after we confirm the full window).

If you can share any additional logs for the req IDs in req_ids-20270505.txt, that will help accelerate correlation. We'll provide another update within 60–90 minutes or sooner if there is a material change.

Sorry for the disruption — we appreciate the quick signal and will prioritize resolution.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
